item.mechanism: Similar mobilities of vacancies and self-interstitials maximize recombination probability, minimizing defect cluster formation and reducing precipitation kinetics.
item.system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy (38% W, 36% Ta, 15% Cr, 11% V)
item.operating_conditions: Irradiation at 1073 K and room temperature up to 8 dpa; nanocrystalline grains (≤100 nm)
item.supporting_observation: No dislocation loops observed even at 8 dpa, contrasting with pure W where defect mobilities differ greatly.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold in pure W where there is a great disparity in defect mobilities; effect of precipitates on recombination probability noted as not large at low temperatures.
item.alternatives_considered: Dislocation loop formation and clustering due to disparate defect mobilities (as seen in pure W).
quotes: The fact that no clustering is experimentally observed indicates that, in the HEA described in this work, this is a plausible case, i.e., the mobilities of vacancies and self-interstitials are similar
Maximizing recombination will lead to a reduction in defect concentration and therefore a reduction in the kinetics of precipitation and growth of second-phase particles.
Equal mobilities must be a consequence of the rough energy landscape induced by the local lattice distortion and the disparity in chemistry.

item.mechanism: Thermodynamic driving force for phase separation leads to Cr- and V-rich precipitate formation rather than dislocation loop accumulation.
item.system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy (38% W, 36% Ta, 15% Cr, 11% V)
item.operating_conditions: Annealing up to 1073 K; irradiation at 1073 K and room temperature; as-deposited state
item.supporting_observation: First-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations show strong segregation tendency of Cr and V, reproducing the Cr-V-rich precipitates observed experimentally.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the thermodynamic stability of this specific quaternary composition; kinetic effects may cause slight compositional differences between simulation and experiment.
item.alternatives_considered: Random solid solution stability; formation of dislocation loops instead of precipitates.
quotes: The results of this modeling analysis, showing the phase separation of Cr-V–rich precipitates, are fully consistent with the compositional layering features observed in the APT results
The fact that precipitation is also observed under irradiation is also consistent with the modeling results that highlight a strong thermodynamic force for the system to phase separate.

item.mechanism: Grain boundaries act as preferential recombination/annihilation sites for defects, reducing defect concentrations within the grains.
item.system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy with bimodal grain size distribution (~70% ≤100 nm)
item.operating_conditions: Irradiation at 1073 K and room temperature; presence of high density of grain boundaries
item.supporting_observation: Defect clusters are not observed in the HEA, attributed to minimized defect concentrations inside grains due to boundary recombination.
item.scope_limits: Nanocrystalline W with similar grain sizes still shows large dislocation loops, indicating this mechanism alone is insufficient without the mobility equalization effect.
item.alternatives_considered: Defect accumulation and loop formation despite high grain boundary density (as seen in nanocrystalline W).
quotes: The presence of a high density of grain boundaries will also lead to a reduction of the defect concentrations, as grain boundaries are usually preferential recombination/annihilation sites for defects.
The fact that defect clusters are not observed in the HEA leads again to the fact that the concentration of defects inside the grains is minimized by the fact that their mobilities are similar.
However, even nanocrystalline W with grain sizes on the order of the ones studied here shows the formation of large irradiation-created dislocation loops that diffuse to grain boundaries.

item.mechanism: Local lattice distortion and chemical disparity create a rough energy landscape that equalizes defect mobilities.
item.operating_conditions: General alloy state; underlying cause for radiation tolerance observed during irradiation
item.supporting_observation: The authors infer that the observed lack of clustering and equal defect mobilities are consequences of the rough energy landscape.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the chemical complexity and lattice distortion inherent to this high-entropy alloy system.
item.alternatives_considered: Uniform energy landscape leading to disparate defect mobilities (as in pure W).
quotes: Equal mobilities must be a consequence of the rough energy landscape induced by the local lattice distortion and the disparity in chemistry.

The configurational entropy of mixing in multicomponent alloys tends to stabilize the solid solution based on simple underlying face-centered cubic (FCC) or body-centered cubic (BCC) crystal structures.
Chemical complexity can lead to a variation in the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of defects that might modify the microstructure evolution under irradiation.

item.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and dispersion strengthening from precipitates improve mechanical properties (hardness/strength).
item.operating_conditions: As-deposited, annealed, and irradiated states; hardness measured via nanoindentation
item.supporting_observation: Hardness of ~15 GPa observed; slight increase after annealing and irradiation, attributed to precipitation and solid solution effects.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the quaternary system studied; other W-based HEAs with different compositions (e.g., quinary) showed twofold improvement due to similar mechanisms.
item.alternatives_considered: Hardness increase solely due to irradiation hardening without precipitation contribution.
quotes: These materials can display high hardness values, high yield strengths, large ductility, excellent fatigue resistance, and good fracture toughness.

The authors studied the mechanical response, showing that these materials could lead to twofold improvement in the hardness and strength due to solid solution strengthening and dispersion strengthening.
The annealing process results in a hardness increase, which is slightly enhanced by irradiation.

item.mechanism: Negative enthalpies of mixing for specific binary pairs (W-Ta, W-V, Cr-V) drive atomic ordering and segregation.
item.operating_conditions: Thermodynamic equilibrium calculations at various temperatures (e.g., 1000 K)
item.supporting_observation: DFT/CE calculations show negative enthalpies for W-Ta, W-V, and Cr-V binaries, indicating a tendency for segregation or ordering.
item.scope_limits: Does not apply to binaries with positive enthalpies of mixing (e.g., Ta-V, Cr-W) which favor mixing or different behaviors.
item.alternatives_considered: Positive enthalpies of mixing leading to random mixing or phase separation in different directions.
quotes: The positive and negative enthalpies of mixing values indicate a tendency for segregation or ordering, respectively.
For the Cr-Ta system, besides the small negative enthalpies of mixing, again due to mixing between elements of the two groups, there are also positive values.

item.mechanism: Elemental segregation to grain boundaries and triple junctions occurs due to thermodynamic driving forces, influencing microstructure stability.
item.operating_conditions: As-deposited, annealed at 1050 K, and irradiated states
item.supporting_observation: APT analysis confirms segregation of Cr and V to grain boundaries and triple junctions in both as-deposited and irradiated samples.
item.scope_limits: Not all grains demonstrated compositional clustering, indicating grain variations regarding elemental segregation.
item.alternatives_considered: Homogeneous distribution of elements or disappearance of compositional striations upon heating.
quotes: APT results show the segregation of Cr and V to grain boundaries and triple junctions.
We also found evidence for element segregations to the grain boundaries, as shown in the three distinct grain boundaries captured by APT.

item.mechanism: High-Z elements are selected to minimize sputtering, while low-activation elements are chosen to reduce radiotoxicity.
item.system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy (selected from exclusion of Ni, Cu, Al, Mo, Co, Nb, Fe, Mn)
item.operating_conditions: Material selection criteria for fusion plasma-facing applications
item.supporting_observation: The authors explicitly state the exclusion criteria for alloying elements based on sputtering and radiotoxicity concerns.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the selection process for fusion reactor components; does not describe a physical mechanism of radiation resistance itself but a design constraint.
item.alternatives_considered: Use of Ni, Cu, Al, Mo, Co, Nb (excluded due to radiotoxicity) or Fe, Mn (excluded due to intermetallic formation).
quotes: To narrow the possible candidate systems, we have to bear in mind that high-Z materials are generally desirable to minimize sputtering.
In addition, low-activation elements must be considered to reduce radiotoxicity, which excludes the use of Ni, Cu, Al, Mo, Co, or Nb.
Furthermore, Fe and Mn usually form intermetallics, which might induce a more complex behavior. Thus, W, Ta, V, and Cr were chosen as testing ingredients for the target system.
